description.ncbi_summary: Microsomal arylacetamide deacetylase competes against the activity of cytosolic arylamine N-acetyltransferase, which catalyzes one of the initial biotransformation pathways for arylamine and heterocyclic amine carcinogens [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of ester and amide bonds and is largely involved in prodrugs activation, xenobiotic detoxification or toxicity, and, in some contexts, lipid and indole metabolism (PubMed:17936933, PubMed:18034159, PubMed:19339378, PubMed:2043131, PubMed:21856291, PubMed:22207054, PubMed:22415931, PubMed:23542347, PubMed:24125761, PubMed:24464802, PubMed:26164127, PubMed:27422753, PubMed:33446525, PubMed:34450168, PubMed:37002641, PubMed:8063807). Prefers compounds with relatively small acyl groups, especially compounds with acetyl group (PubMed:26164127). Participates in the hydrolysis of clinical drugs including acetyl esters compounds such as eslicarbazepine, abiraterone and rifamycins (rifampicin, rifabutin, and rifapentine) and N-acetylarylamine compounds such as flutamide, N-monoacetyldapsone, and phenacetin (PubMed:19339378, PubMed:21856291, PubMed:22207054, PubMed:22415931, PubMed:24125761, PubMed:24464802, PubMed:26164127, PubMed:27422753). Participates in the hydrolysis of carcinogen such as 2-acetylaminofluorene (AAF) and propanil (PubMed:2043131, PubMed:26164127, PubMed:8063807). In addition, plays a role in lipid metabolism by hydrolyzing newly synthesized diacylglycerol, so limiting triacylglycerol synthesis for cytoplasmic storage droplet formation and for VLDL assembly (PubMed:23542347). Can also catalyzes the deacetylation of cholesterol acetate (PubMed:18034159). Moreover can play a role in metabolism of pineal indoles by catalyzing the deacetylation of N-acetylarylalkylamine compounds including N-acetylserotonin (NAS), melatonin and N-acetyltryptamine, NAS conversion being the most efficient reaction (PubMed:37002641).
